sources: Keyframe templates adapted from the R4 everyday tasks (public/data/tasks.json, from prototype/index.html EX/CH); depths are scaled by the generator to reach each target (plan 2b.9). Angles are start values chosen for the app, not measured.
Stoop vs squat lifting: van Dieen JH, Hoozemans MJM, Toussaint HM. Stoop or squat: a review of biomechanical studies on lifting technique. Clin Biomech 1999;14(10):685-696.
Golfer's lift (one leg extended back as a counterweight): McGill S. Low Back Disorders, 2nd ed. Human Kinetics 2007.
One-hand vs two-hand carrying: McGill SM, Marshall L, Andersen J. Low back loads while walking and carrying: comparing the load carried in one hand or in both hands. Ergonomics 2013;56(2):293-302.

Pushing and pulling: Hoozemans MJM, van der Beek AJ, Frings-Dresen MHW, van Dijk FJH, van der Woude LHV. Pushing and pulling in relation to musculoskeletal disorders: a review of risk factors. Ergonomics 1998;41(6):757-781.
Stair climbing: Nadeau S, McFadyen BJ, Malouin F. Frontal and sagittal plane analyses of the stair climbing task in healthy adults aged over 40 years. Clin Biomech 2003;18(10):950-959.
Sit to stand: Schenkman M, Berger RA, Riley PO, Mann RW, Hodge WA. Whole-body movements during rising to standing from sitting. Phys Ther 1990;70(10):638-648.
Object sizes and grip points: public/data/equipment.json objects (same numbers); object masses are approximate start values, not verified (the user sets the weight).
Start heights: table 0.75 m, shelf 1.5 m, overhead 1.9 m (plan 2b.9); knee 0.47 m = the male model's knee height in prototype coordinates.
note: Prototype coordinates (metres, ROOT_Y 0.965) x body scale s. Start: height, forward (+z, in front), side (+x = the body's left). An object's grips are its equipment.json grip points in item coordinates (the object stands at the start). Props: hands both = the object id (load at hands, split over both hands), hands right = object id + R (load at hand_r). free = the prototype keys the generator scales together (one scalar, 0..1 of the template) to reach the target; target.keyframes = which keyframes must reach it. A keyframe with pin none is carried by the style's support prop (supports.json). rest = a body point the free hand rests on in the target keyframes. from: put down and stand up replay their base action reversed; bend and hold keeps the base's first keyframe only. Carry: the target is the two-feet keyframe; in the one-leg keyframe the arms hang as they fall. A templated combination whose grip the hands cannot reach (a high grip on the shelf or overhead; a floor grip in the squat, which keeps the trunk within 20 degrees, or the golfer's lift) is disabled as out of reach. Presets: the five R4 tasks (mop = bend and hold with the mop).

styles.name: Bend at the waist
styles.source: van Dieen 1999 (stoop: knees nearly straight, the hips and spine bend)

styles.name: Squat down
styles.source: van Dieen 1999 (squat: hips, knees and ankles bend, trunk near upright, here at most 18 degrees)

styles.name: One hand, other hand on the knee
styles.source: R4 tasks.json bucket/onehand; stoop with one arm, the other hand braced on the knee (plan 2b.9)

styles.name: Golfer's lift
styles.source: McGill 2007 (golfer's lift: hinge on one leg, the other leg extends back)

styles.name: Split between both hands
styles.source: R4 tasks.json carry/both; McGill 2013 (load split over both hands)

styles.name: Lean in, drive with the legs
styles.source: Hoozemans 1998 (pushing: lean into the load, staggered stance)

styles.name: Stand upright, push with the arms
styles.source: Hoozemans 1998 (pushing at hand height about 1 m; the trunk bends only as far as the hands need to reach)

styles.name: Lean back, drive with the legs
styles.source: Hoozemans 1998 (pulling: lean back away from the load)

styles.name: Stand upright, pull with the arms
styles.source: Hoozemans 1998 (pulling at hand height about 1 m; the trunk bends only as far as the hands need to reach)

styles.name: Upright
styles.source: R4 tasks.json stairs/one; Nadeau 2003 (lead foot on the step, trunk near upright)

styles.name: Lean forward
styles.source: R4 tasks.json stairs/one with more trunk lean; Nadeau 2003

styles.name: Upright
styles.source: Schenkman 1990 (sitting: hips and knees near 90 degrees, trunk upright)

styles.name: Lean forward, arms forward
styles.source: Schenkman 1990 (trunk flexes forward to bring the body over the feet; arms forward as a counterweight)

styles.name: Both hands
styles.source: R4 tasks.json shelf/close (stand close, arms raise to the target; bend at the hips only as far as a low target needs)

presets.name: Put a box on a high shelf
